title: 2017 IDSA Clinical Practice Guidelines for Healthcare-Associated Ventriculitis and Meningitis (Tunkel et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases)

claims.text: In healthcare-associated ventriculitis/meningitis the likely etiologic agents differ from community-acquired disease, being resistant gram-negative bacilli and staphylococci.
CSF shunt infections are commonly caused by coagulase-negative staphylococci and Propionibacterium acnes, which are indolent and evoke minimal inflammation.
claims.byte_quote: coagulase-negative staphylococci and _P. acnes_, are indolent, evoke minimal inflammation

claims.text: Organisms implicated include S. aureus, a coagulase-negative staphylococcus, or Propionibacterium acnes.
claims.byte_quote: _S. aureus_, a coagulase-negative staphylococcus, or _Propionibacterium acnes_

claims.text: Gram-negative bacilli and S. aureus are among the causative organisms.
Host/risk factors raising CSF shunt infection risk include premature birth (especially with intraventricular hemorrhage), younger age, and previous shunt infection.
claims.byte_quote: Factors associated with an increased risk of CSF shunt infection include premature birth (especially when associated with intraventricular hemorrhage), younger age, previous shunt infection

claims.text: Shunt infection risk depends on the cause of hydrocephalus, being more likely after purulent meningitis, hemorrhage, and myelomeningocele.
claims.byte_quote: cause of hydrocephalus (more likely after purulent meningitis, hemorrhage, and myelomeningocele)

claims.text: Procedural/exposure risk factors include less experienced neurosurgeon, more people traversing the operating theater, and exposure to perforated surgical gloves.
claims.byte_quote: less experienced neurosurgeon, higher number of people traversing the operating theater, exposure to perforated surgical gloves

claims.text: Additional procedural risk factors include intraoperative use of the neuroendoscope and longer duration of the shunt procedure.
claims.byte_quote: intraoperative use of the neuroendoscope, longer duration of the shunt procedure

claims.text: Risk factors for infection (drain/device context) include intraventricular or subarachnoid hemorrhage, cranial fracture with CSF leak, catheter irrigation, and craniotomy.
claims.byte_quote: Factors associated with an increased risk of infection are intraventricular or subarachnoid hemorrhage, cranial fracture with CSF leak, catheter irrigation, craniotomy

claims.text: A negative CSF Gram stain does not exclude infection, especially after prior antimicrobial therapy.
claims.byte_quote: A negative CSF Gram stain does not exclude the presence of infection, especially in patients who have received previous antimicrobial therapy

claims.text: Gram-stain diagnostic accuracy depends on the number of organisms present, the type of meningeal pathogen, and receipt of prior antimicrobial therapy.
claims.byte_quote: The diagnostic accuracy of a Gram stain is a function of the number of microorganisms present, the type of meningeal pathogen, and the receipt of prior antimicrobial therapy

claims.text: In one study of nosocomial meningitis the CSF Gram stain was positive in 65 (71%) of 91 cases.
claims.byte_quote: The CSF Gram stain was positive in 65 (71%) of 91 cases in one study of patients with nosocomial meningitis
